clue.text: Hastily assembled during the night? The elves did this!

definitions.text: Hastily assembled during the night? The elves did this!

parts.words: Hastily assembled during the night? The elves did this!
parts.note: the fairy tale of the elves and the shoemaker: elves secretly made shoes overnight, so they literally did a cobbler's work while the shoemaker slept

explanation.surface: A rushed bit of overnight work, blamed on helpful elves.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Grimm tale the elves make shoes at night for a poor shoemaker; mending shoes is a cobbler's job, so their work was literally cobbled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something put together quickly and crudely, and also suggests shoemaking work.

clue.text: Macho Aussie turns up in Berwick-upon-Tweed nude lido. Cor! Cripes!

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tough Australian is spotted at a naked swimming pool in a Northumberland town, to the onlookers' astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is the signal that the answer lies within the following words. In a down clue 'turns up' means read upwards. A lido is an open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the 1986 film is a rugged Australian bushman, the very image of outback toughness.

clue.text: British tech "average" — leader in Times that merits just a few lines

parts.note: IT, information technology, is tech
par is the average or normal standard

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial about British technology that deserves only a brief mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a newspaper editorial in The Times, but it only asks for that word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small acting role has only a handful of spoken lines in a play or film.

clue.text: Play king, punching Liberal Arab unconscious

indicators.note: the king letter punches its way into the Liberal-plus-Arab string, ending up inside it

parts.note: taken as a word
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
someone knocked out cold is out

explanation.surface: A monarch hits a Liberal and an Arab until they are knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punching' and 'unconscious' paint a violent scene, but the answer means to fool around.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around or behave playfully, which is to play.

clue.text: Burgess's thug runs over to be bitten by hound

indicators.note: being bitten means being held in the hound's jaws, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a hound is a dog
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A thug runs off only to be bitten by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Burgess's novel A Clockwork Orange calls its young thugs by this word in its invented slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In A Clockwork Orange the narrator's gang members are called by this slang word for a friend or henchman.

clue.text: Kissed very large copper behind back of Yard

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very large
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means behind time

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of Yard

explanation.surface: A burly policeman steals a kiss behind Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'Yard' suggest a police officer at Scotland Yard, but copper is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word for to kiss, from Latin osculum, a little mouth.

clue.text: Bug that is set up to trap senior army officer

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the officer goes between the reversed letters
in a down clue set up means placed upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A trap is set to catch a high-ranking army officer, like a spy sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' may suggest a listening device in a spy trap; here it is a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common gut bacterium, and bug is the informal word for an infectious microbe.

clue.text: Slick product introduced to Barnet

parts.note: Barnet is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and a slick product is something applied to slick it down

explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is also a London borough, so it reads like a new product launched there; in Cockney rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grooming preparation rubbed into the hair to make it glossy and smooth.

clue.text: Dodgy USA-run lotteries a risky venture

indicators.note: dodgy means crooked or unreliable, so the letters are rigged into a new order

explanation.surface: Crooked American-run lotteries are a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: Russian roulette means firing a revolver with one loaded chamber at oneself; figuratively, any reckless gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used figuratively for any dangerous gamble with potentially disastrous consequences.

clue.text: Don't start riot when fully exposed here in Canada

indicators.note: each of the three words is stripped of its outer covering, losing its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A plea not to begin a riot by streaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' looks like an instruction to drop the first letter of one word; in fact all three words lose both ends, giving ON, TAR and IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a province of Canada, so it is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Conservative corrupted senior close friends

indicators.note: corrupted means debased, so these letters are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: A senior Tory has been led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue hints at cronyism among politicians, which the answer itself names.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronies are intimate companions or chums, often with a hint of favouritism.

clue.text: Midwest city mom embraced by old husband back in Nebraska

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside the old-husband pair

parts.note: mom is American for mother, ma

indicators.note: the back of Nebraska is its final letter

explanation.surface: An American mother is hugged by her elderly husband on returning home to Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in Nebraska' reads like returning home, but only asks for the last letter of Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, a state in the American Midwest.

clue.text: US soldier saving everybody I cut when retreating in battle

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so the soldier's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: GI is the slang term for an American soldier
all means everybody

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: An American soldier rescues everyone, though wounded as he falls back in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the 1915-16 First World War campaign in which Allied forces failed to take the Dardanelles.

clue.text: A shy person, fashionable model Trevor retires

parts.note: in means fashionable
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so a model can be T

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: Trevor, a bashful fashion model, decides to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable model' looks like one phrase about a catwalk model; split it into IN and T, the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is someone reserved and inward-looking, typically quiet and retiring in company.

clue.text: Knight avoids close shave involving large human being

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the large letter goes inside
avoiding means keeping away, so the knight's letter is dropped

parts.note: a near thing is a close shave, a narrow escape
N is the chess notation for a knight
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A knight narrowly escapes a nasty incident with something big.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping N from NEAR THING leaves EARTHING, which then takes L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction an earthling is a person from our planet, a member of humankind.

clue.text: Business occasionally seen in small towns?

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A firm that crops up now and again in little towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a shop or establishment such as a hairdresser's or beauty parlour, a type of business.

clue.text: Thus radical Islamic political ideology?

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: radical means drastic change, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Is radical Islam therefore a political ideology?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical Islamic' reads as a political label, but radical rearranges the letters of Islamic.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialism is a political doctrine favouring collective or state ownership of the means of production.

clue.text: Dislodge England's opener, caught during ITV broadcast

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here of England
during means within the span of, so the caught letter goes inside
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman is caught out in a match shown on ITV, a British television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' and 'caught' suggest a cricket dismissal on television; the ITV letters become VIT and take C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel someone from a property, forcing them out.

clue.text: One million soldiers on both sides of square that's vast

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A million troops line a parade ground, an enormous force.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, enormous in size or extent.

clue.text: Italian leaves a chic Dior collection

indicators.note: a fashion collection is a new assembly of designs, so these letters are put together in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Leaves on display in a stylish Dior fashion line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collection' fits Dior's fashion range, and 'Italian leaves' sounds like people departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved Italian chicory used in salads.

clue.text: Try Fifth Ave — a gorgeous surrounding

indicators.note: the words given wrap round the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample the luxury of New York's Fifth Avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts with the last letter of Fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is an informal idiom for making an attempt.

clue.text: Peerless article in French magazine from Paris editor

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
Paris Match is a French weekly magazine

explanation.surface: A superb piece in a French magazine by a Paris editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmatched means without equal, so nothing can rival or compare with it.

clue.text: Bones of sailors found on island

parts.note: tars are sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen's skeletons discovered on a desert island.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle and upper foot.

clue.text: Doctor Green installed home furnishings

indicators.note: installed means fitted inside, so the green letters go within

parts.note: eco- means environmentally green

explanation.surface: A doctor fits environmentally friendly fittings in their home.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of a room's furnishing and decoration.

clue.text: Hard fixture where the Hammers will strike?

definitions.text: Hard fixture where the Hammers will strike?

parts.words: Hard fixture where the Hammers will strike?
parts.note: West Ham United are nicknamed the Hammers, so this reads like a tough match; literally, it is a solid fixed block that hammers strike

explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United are a London football club nicknamed the Hammers, so 'hard fixture' reads as a tough game for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's heavy iron block, on which metal is hammered into shape.

clue.text: Coins retroactive term for rudimentary bomb Iran planted

indicators.note: retroactive means working backwards, so the whole combination is read in reverse
planted means set inside, so the country's name goes into the bomb's letters

parts.note: IED, improvised explosive device, is the term for a crude homemade bomb

explanation.surface: A news story about Iran planting crude bombs, with an odd mention of coins.
explanation.walkthrough: IED stands for improvised explosive device. 'Retroactive' applies to the whole assembly, after the country has been planted, not just to the bomb term.
explanation.definitionFit: Denarii were silver coins of ancient Rome; the singular is denarius.

clue.text: Graphic images upset April in court

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the court's letters
upset means knocked over, so the month's letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Pictures shown in court one April cause distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip art is ready-made illustrations supplied for pasting into documents.

clue.text: Herbal remedy enlivening pensioner Reg with vim?

indicators.note: enlivening means livening up, so these letters are stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A herbal tonic that gives an elderly man called Reg fresh energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening primrose oil, pressed from the plant's seeds, is a popular herbal supplement.
